newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down as liquidity eases.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down as liquidity eases.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down a hefty 225 basis points at a session low of 29.00 percent on Tuesday, following the central bank's announcement that it would ease its liquidity target to cero from minus 20 million pesos, traders said.
"The liquidity target was a great help. Liquidity began to run short yesterday with banks demanding liquidity to settle checking accounts they hold with the central bank," said a trader.
Banks have to settle these accounts by Wednesday.
Liquidity pressures had previously driven the overnight rate to a high of 31.40 percent.
Banco de Mexico's liquidity target of minus 20 million pesos had been in force since October 14.
"We were expecting Banco de Mexico to return to its zero target, as the peso has been stable for a while now," another trader said.
Traders in general felt that easing liquidity requirements would allow primary rates to fall at the Cetes auction later in the day.

A Reuters survey of 10 money market traders showed they expected Banco de Mexico to assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at an average of 29.41 percent, which would be 44 basis points down from last week's auction.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 190 basis points at 30.10 percent.
Banco de Mexico injected 3.995 billion pesos into the secondary market by auctioning three credits, which it assigned at between 30.80 and 31.18 percent.
Total credit maturities were estimated at 7.628 billion pesos for Wednesday.
